basics.name: Brice Rigourd
basics.label: Energy engineer and Python developer
basics.summary: Energy engineer (solar PV, wind, grid connection) who builds the Python tools that replace manual work for technical teams. ESTIA engineer with a Master's in Smart Grids from the University of the Basque Country (UPV/EHU). I write the software that replaces manual work for technical teams: tools that read thousands of PDFs, desktop applications, Excel/VBA tools and AI prototypes. I have delivered tools to Amarenco (solar power producer), to Energiter (wind and solar engineering consultancy) and for a medical-device manufacturer.

work.name: Amarenco
work.summary: Operations of a portfolio of 287 PV plants at the end of the assignment (14 SPVs, 67.3 MWp, mostly rooftop) and development of the team's automation tools.
highlights: Plant performance monitoring (performance ratio, expected yield) in the 3E SynaptiQ monitoring platform.
Monthly reports to shareholders, KPI and OPEX budget tracking, Asset Management and O&M contracts.
About 18,000 lines of Python in the final versions of the team's tools; typed package (mypy --strict, ruff, black, pytest).
Feedback from a user about the automated analysis of maintenance reports (translated from French): "an absolutely brilliant tool".

PVsyst ↔ SynaptiQ quality control (March – June 2025) : Check PVsyst studies against each plant's digital twin in SynaptiQ to explain inconsistent performance ratios: misconfigured twin, wrong PVsyst simulation, or both.

PVsyst orchestrator (July – September 2025) : My first Python application with a graphical interface, built to keep the internal technical database up to date with the new PVsyst studies uploaded to SharePoint every week by internal and external design offices.

work.name: Energiter
work.summary: Wind and solar feasibility studies, yield referent, and development of a grid connection study tool.
highlights: Over 40 PV feasibility and yield studies: MV-connected plants from 2 to 22 MWp, PVsyst with Solargis data.
Over 15 wind simulations in WAsP and windPRO: 3 to 15 MW wind farms, ERA5 and MERRA data.
Grid connection studies for RTE and Enedis source substations.
Bat-curtailment method in windPRO, validated against the in-house Python tool (about one point of difference on two wind farms).
Grid connection study tool (Master's thesis subject) (April – September 2024) : Find the best source substation to connect a wind or solar farm, from public grid data.

work.name: Ezio Industrial Consulting
work.summary: Assignment for a medical-device manufacturer (cold-plasma sterilization): design and delivery of a complete application, from requirements to user manual.
highlights: Training documents on machine capability, qualifications and ISO 13485.
PlasmaCraft, recipe-authoring software (May – August 2023) : Excel/VBA software for authoring the machine's PLC recipes, designed from scratch.

projects.name: PVsyst ↔ SynaptiQ quality control
projects.description: Check PVsyst studies against each plant's digital twin in SynaptiQ to explain inconsistent performance ratios: misconfigured twin, wrong PVsyst simulation, or both.
highlights: About 154,000 SharePoint documents inventoried across 4,660 projects; about 7,500 PVsyst files kept (latest version of each project).
Full extraction of the SynaptiQ API: 970 active plants, 1,794 module groups, 4,383 inverters.
Automated comparison: tilt/azimuth pairs (identical, within ±1° or ±10°), module count per pair and five losses; matching by project code or by name.

Over 230 PVsyst studies with discrepancies reported to the teams, over a hundred being redone; mostly orientation discrepancies (azimuth in the wrong cardinal direction) and module counts per orientation.

projects.name: PVsyst orchestrator
projects.description: My first Python application with a graphical interface, built to keep the internal technical database up to date with the new PVsyst studies uploaded to SharePoint every week by internal and external design offices.
highlights: Read-only SharePoint connection; the latest PVsyst studies of each SPV are located and downloaded into a local database, with an archive of older versions.
Multiprocess extraction of PVsyst v6 to v8 reports, in French and English, then comparison with the internal technical database: missing or outdated data, by SPV and project code.
Project status checks (cancelled, renamed, merged SPVs) and three Excel control workbooks to verify the tool's work.
Full update in 1 to 10 minutes instead of 2 to 3 weeks by hand; simple check in 10 seconds to 5 minutes; first download of a portfolio of more than 300 plants in 30 minutes to 1 h 20.
Validated and used from time to time by 3 fellow engineers, then handed by the department to a development team for internal deployment.
Batch analyses: 26,809 DC/AC ratios extracted and 2,051 plants sorted into six clipping-risk classes; 2,150 grid access contracts read.

projects.name: Grid connection study tool (Master's thesis subject)
projects.description: Find the best source substation to connect a wind or solar farm, from public grid data.
highlights: Over 3,400 source substations filtered by downstream voltage (20 kV or more) and ranked by a 0-to-5 criticality score, in 5 to 20 seconds.
Real road distance through the IGN routing API called asynchronously: about 64% less response time.

Caparéseau (RTE) capacities and S3REnR regional schemes downloaded and archived; analysis with and without reinforcement works; costing in 17 MW modules, cable choice, network cost and regional cost share.
Deliverables: KML for Google Earth, folium maps, a project database and a PDF report; Excel/VBA interface driving the Python scripts through PowerShell.

projects.name: PlasmaCraft, recipe-authoring software
projects.description: Excel/VBA software for authoring the machine's PLC recipes, designed from scratch.
highlights: 53 VBA modules, about 4,750 lines, 115 procedures.
Recipes of up to 100 sequences with four parameters controlled over time; input checks against the machine's limits and step size (0 to 3,600 s per sequence, 0 to 500 W, 0 to 5 sccm, 0 to 22 G).
Ramps split into 5 to 25 steps that add up exactly; batch editing; TXT export for the PLC and locked XLSM recipes.
All nine client requirements covered; a 33-page user manual and an installation guide; name and logo designed and approved by the client.

projects.name: Combat agent trained in simulation (test bed: AION 2)
projects.description: An agent that reads the game screen and decides every action, trained first by imitation, then in a simulated arena.
highlights: 640×360 capture at 7 frames per second, detection in about 3 ms without a GPU.
Imitation learning on 1,864 examples: 39.4% accuracy against 21.6% for the majority class.
2.5D arena calibrated on the real game; 32 settings trained with the cross-entropy method, validation score from 16.9 to 19.2 out of 20.
PySide6 Windows application, about 29,000 lines of Python and 740 pytest tests; external approach only, simulation mode by default.

projects.name: Pulse, a dating app
projects.description: Full-stack Android app, from prototype to release 1.014.
highlights: Expo SDK 54, React Native 0.81 and TypeScript; FastAPI and WebSocket server; Supabase database migrated from MongoDB.
Photos on S3 storage through presigned URLs, with a hand-written SigV4 signature.
About 70 API routes, 16,800 lines of TypeScript and 5,400 lines of server code, 135 commits.
Developed with Claude and Claude Code after a prototype built with the Emergent agent.

projects.name: Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W as a USB mouse and keyboard
projects.description: A microcontroller that poses as a USB mouse and keyboard and draws in Paint, driven by a Python script.
highlights: CircuitPython and USB HID; commands received over a serial port.
Closed-loop control from the cursor's real position; Paint buttons located through UI Automation.
About 680 lines of Python.

projects.name: KidsVid, AI-generated videos for children, made locally
projects.description: A 100% local, open-source pipeline producing narrated stories and nursery rhymes, in French and English.
highlights: n8n orchestrates a FastAPI service chaining Ollama and Qwen3, Piper, SDXL through ComfyUI, ACE-Step and FFmpeg.
About 2,100 lines of Python, 19 API routes, 3 n8n workflows.
Lessons: licenses compatible with commercial use, YouTube's "inauthentic content" policy, COPPA obligations.
